sounds.name: Talking Lead
sounds.blurb: A gliding two-saw lead through a narrow band that opens and closes like a mouth as the joystick moves.
sounds.how: Wide Band runs a low-pass and a high-pass in a row, WIDTH apart, so only a band round FREQUENCY gets through: with the resonance up it sounds like a vowel. The Filter Width route takes Full On scaled by Joystick Y, so pushing the stick up widens the band and changes the vowel. Mono with auto glide slides between legato notes.

steps.title: Two saws, slightly apart
steps.why:
Both oscillators play their sawtooth, Oscillator 2 a few cents sharp.
- OSC BALANCE 0: both at once.
- CENT 1.5: a slow beating between them.
- Listen for: a thick, moving saw.

steps.title: A band, not a slope
steps.why:
Wide Band keeps only the band between the two filters.
- MODE to Wide Band.
- FREQUENCY 6, WIDTH 2, RESONANCE 6: a narrow, peaky band round 1.3 kHz.
- Listen for: a nasal, vocal tone.

steps.title: The joystick on the width
steps.why:
The Filter Width route: Full On, multiplied by Joystick Y, at WIDTH MOD's depth.
- CONTROL Filter Width, SOURCE Full On, SCALE Joystick Y.
- WIDTH MOD 4.
- Joystick pushed up to 0.6.
- Listen for: the band opening into a wider 'ah'. Move the stick to make it talk.

steps.title: One voice that glides
steps.why:
- VOICING Mono (both buttons off).
- GLIDE 4, AUTO lit: only legato notes slide.
- Listen for: the line sliding up into its long notes.

tweaks.try: Pull the joystick back to the centre

tweaks.try: Step MODE on to Wide Notch
tweaks.hear: The band turns inside out: the middle is cut and the rest gets through.

sounds.name: Notch Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of progressive rock
sounds.blurb: A hollow saw-and-pulse lead with a slow, swirling cut through its middle.
sounds.how: Wide Notch takes a slice out of the sound rather than keeping one. LFO 1 sweeps the notch's FREQUENCY through the Filter Freq route, so the missing slice moves slowly up and down, a little like a phaser.

steps.title: A saw and a pulse
steps.why:
- OSC BALANCE 0: both oscillators.
- OSC 2 WAVE pulse, SHAPE 3: a fairly narrow pulse.
- Listen for: a bright, reedy blend.

steps.title: Cut a notch
steps.why:
- MODE to Wide Notch.
- FREQUENCY 5, RESONANCE 3.
- Listen for: a hollow sound, its middle taken out.

steps.title: Sweep the notch
steps.why:
The Filter Freq route, its source changed from Envelope 2 to LFO 1.
- CONTROL Filter Freq, SOURCE LFO 1.
- FREQ MOD 2, LFO 1 RATE 3: a slow sweep of over two octaves.
- Listen for: the hollow moving up and down.

steps.title: Let the notes ring
steps.why:
- Envelope 1 RELEASE 4.
- Listen for: each note fading out under the next.

context.vcf.cutoffMod: In this sound: how far the notch sweeps.
context.lfo1.rate: In this sound: the speed of the sweep.

tweaks.hear: The swirl speeds up into a fast, watery phasing.

sounds.name: Duophonic Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s duophonic synth leads
sounds.blurb: A two-note band-pass lead: play two keys and each gets a voice, and a filter, of its own.
sounds.how: Duophonic voicing gives each of two held notes one of the Mantis's two analogue paths. In the 12 dB modes each path has its own filter, so a melody in thirds keeps both lines clear. The band-pass gives the narrow, singing tone.

steps.title: Two voices
steps.why:
- MONO / DUO lit: Duophonic.
- Listen for: two keys held give two notes; a third steals one.

steps.title: A pulse
steps.why:
- OSC 1 WAVE pulse, SHAPE 3.
- Listen for: a hollow, reedy tone.

steps.title: Band-pass at 12 dB
steps.why:
In the 12 dB types each voice path gets a filter of its own.
- MODE to BP12.
- FREQUENCY 6, RESONANCE 4.
- Listen for: a narrow, singing band on each note.

steps.title: Release and chorus
steps.why:
- Envelope 1 RELEASE 3.
- CHORUS LEVEL 3.
- Listen for: the two lines spreading a little wider.

context.kbd.voicing: In this sound: two notes at once, one per path.
context.vcf.cutoff: In this sound: where the band sits.

tweaks.try: Press MONO / DUO again for Mono
tweaks.hear: Only one note of each pair plays.
A thin, buzzy pair of lines with the lows taken out.

sounds.name: Density Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of ambient music
sounds.blurb: A wide, slowly breathing four-voice pad, thickened by the density oscillator and washed in chorus and reverb.
sounds.how: DENSITY adds a detuned copy of Oscillator 2 under it, so every note beats like a pair of oscillators. Envelope 2 opens the filter slowly through the Filter Freq route, and the chorus and reverb spread the voices out.

steps.title: Two saws and a density copy
steps.why:
- OSC BALANCE 0.
- DENSITY 7, DENSITY RATE 4: a copy of Oscillator 2 a few cents off.
- Listen for: a slow, chorus-like beating on every note.

steps.title: A slow filter
steps.why:
The Filter Freq route starts on Envelope 2.
- FREQUENCY 5.
- FREQ MOD 2.
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 7, DECAY 7, SUSTAIN 6, RELEASE 7.
- Listen for: each chord opening up slowly.

steps.title: A soft loudness
steps.why:
- Envelope 1 ATTACK 6, RELEASE 7.
- Listen for: chords that swell in and fade away.

steps.title: Chorus and reverb
steps.why:
- CHORUS LEVEL 6, MODE 2.
- REVERB LEVEL 6, TIME 7.
- Listen for: a wide, distant wash.

context.osc2.densityRate: In this sound: how fast the notes beat.
context.fx.reverbLevel: In this sound: the space round the pad.

tweaks.hear: The beating turns fast and sour, a wide, detuned sound.
The pad thins out and stops shimmering.

sounds.name: Drawbar Organ
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s progressive rock organ
sounds.blurb: A bright organ from the organ wave, an octave above and a sub below, with a fast chorus.
sounds.how: The organ wave, its SHAPE adding harmonics, on both oscillators an octave apart, with the sub under Oscillator 1: three footages, as on a drawbar organ. Envelope 1 is a plain gate, and chorus type 3 gives the swirl.

steps.title: The organ wave
steps.why:
- OSC 1 WAVE organ, SHAPE 6.
- OSC 2 WAVE organ, SHAPE 6, OCTAVE +1.
- OSC BALANCE −2: Oscillator 1 a little louder.
- Listen for: a hollow, organ-like tone with an octave on top.

steps.title: The sub underneath
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SUB LEVEL 6.
- Listen for: a deeper foot under the chord.

steps.title: A quick release and chorus
steps.why:
- Envelope 1 RELEASE 1: the notes stop when the keys do.
- CHORUS LEVEL 5, MODE 3.
- Listen for: a swirling, rotary-like shimmer.

context.osc1.shape: In this sound: how bright the organ is.
context.sub.level: In this sound: the low footage.

tweaks.hear: More harmonics: a brighter, reedier organ.

sounds.name: Wavetable Sweep
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s new wave
sounds.blurb: A glassy tone whose wave itself sweeps on each note, from soft to bright and back.
sounds.how: WT sweeps the wave through a table. The Osc1 Shape route takes Envelope 2, so each note moves through the table and settles part-way, as the wavetable synths of the early 80s did. The filter stays open: the movement is in the wave.

steps.title: Into the wavetable
steps.why:
- OSC 1 WAVE to WT, SHAPE 2.
- Listen for: a soft, rounded wave near the start of the table.

steps.title: Envelope 2 sweeps it
steps.why:
- CONTROL Osc1 Shape, SOURCE Env 2.
- SHAPE MOD 4.
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 3, DECAY 6, SUSTAIN 3, RELEASE 5.
- Listen for: each note brightening as it sweeps through the table, then settling.

steps.title: A little space
steps.why:
- Envelope 1 RELEASE 4.
- REVERB LEVEL 4.
- Listen for: notes that ring into the room.

context.osc1.shapeMod: In this sound: how far each note sweeps through the table.
context.env2.decay: In this sound: how long the sweep takes.

tweaks.hear: The sweep runs the other way, from brighter to softer.

sounds.name: Ring Bells
sounds.ref: In the style of the BBC Radiophonic Workshop
sounds.blurb: Clangy, metallic bells from two sines ring-modulated, dying away into reverb.
sounds.how: The ring modulator multiplies Oscillator 1 by Oscillator 2: with two sines a fifth and an octave apart it gives the sum and difference of the two, which do not fit a simple harmonic series and so sound like a bell. RM BALANCE turned up hears mostly that.

steps.title: Two sines
steps.why:
- OSC 1 WAVE sine, SHAPE 0.
- OSC 2 WAVE sine, SHAPE 0, OCTAVE +1, SEMITONE 7: a twelfth above.
- Listen for: (with RM BALANCE still down) a plain sine.

steps.title: Ring modulate them
steps.why:
- RM BALANCE 8: mostly the ring modulator.
- Listen for: a clangy, metallic tone.

steps.title: A bell's decay
steps.why:
- Envelope 1 DECAY 6, SUSTAIN 0, RELEASE 6.
- Listen for: each strike dying away.

steps.title: Reverb
steps.why:
- REVERB LEVEL 5, TIME 6.
- Listen for: the bells ringing in a hall.

context.mix.ring: In this sound: how much bell there is.
context.osc2.semitone: In this sound: which bell, by the interval between the two sines.

tweaks.hear: A darker, more dissonant bell.
The bell goes and only the plain sine is left.

sounds.name: Acid Line
sounds.ref: In the style of acid house
sounds.blurb: A squelchy, resonant saw bass through the steep low-pass, with drive and a little slide.
sounds.how: One saw into LP24 with the resonance high. The Filter Freq route starts on Envelope 2, so a short Envelope 2 snaps the filter open on every note. DRIVE thickens it, and auto glide slides the tied notes.

steps.title: One voice
steps.why:
- VOICING Mono.
- GLIDE 2, AUTO lit: the tied notes slide.
- Listen for: a single line.

steps.title: A steep, ringing filter
steps.why:
- MODE LP24.
- FREQUENCY 3, RESONANCE 8.
- DRIVE 4.
- Listen for: a dark, peaky, thick saw.

steps.title: Envelope 2 snaps it open
steps.why:
- FREQ MOD 3.5 (the route's source is Envelope 2).
- Envelope 2 DECAY 3, SUSTAIN 0.
- Listen for: the squelch on every note.

context.vcf.cutoffMod: In this sound: the depth of the squelch.

tweaks.hear: The squelch turns into a slower wah.
The filter screams and starts to whistle.

sounds.name: Synced Arp
sounds.blurb: A held chord run as sixteenths over two octaves, its pulse width moving in time with the bar.
sounds.how: ARP plays the held keys upwards over two octaves, one per sixteenth at BPM. Envelope 2 plucks the filter on each note, and LFO 1, synced to a bar, slowly widens and narrows Oscillator 2's pulse, so the pattern changes colour in time.

steps.title: The arpeggiator
steps.why:
- ARP on, ARP MODE Up, OCTAVE 2.
- BPM 6.9 (138), SYNC 7.5 (sixteenths).
- Listen for: the chord running up two octaves.

steps.title: A plucked filter
steps.why:
- FREQUENCY 5, RESONANCE 4, FREQ MOD 3 (from Envelope 2).
- Envelope 2 DECAY 3, SUSTAIN 0.
- Envelope 1 DECAY 3, SUSTAIN 3.
- Listen for: short, plucky notes.

steps.title: A pulse moving with the bar
steps.why:
- OSC BALANCE 0, OSC 2 WAVE pulse.
- SHAPE MOD 3 on Oscillator 2 (its route starts on LFO 2): CONTROL Osc2 Shape, SOURCE LFO 1.
- LFO 1 SYNC to sync, RATE 3: one cycle a bar.
- Listen for: the tone hollowing and filling in time with the pattern.

steps.title: Reverb
steps.why:
- REVERB LEVEL 3.
- Listen for: the notes trailing into the room.

context.arp.octaves: In this sound: how far the pattern climbs.
context.lfo1.rate: In this sound: synced, how many bars the pulse takes to move.

tweaks.hear: The notes of the chord come in a random order.
The pattern runs at half the speed.

sounds.name: PWM Strings
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s string machines
sounds.blurb: Soft, shimmering strings from two pulses whose widths move on two LFOs.
sounds.how: Each oscillator's pulse width moves on an LFO of its own through its shape route (Oscillator 1 on LFO 1, Oscillator 2 on LFO 2, as the routes start), at slightly different speeds, which gives the ensemble shimmer. A slow attack and the chorus finish it.

steps.title: Two pulses
steps.why:
- OSC 1 and OSC 2 WAVE pulse.
- OSC BALANCE 0.
- Listen for: a hollow, square tone.

steps.title: Moving widths
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SHAPE MOD 3, OSC 2 SHAPE MOD 3.
- LFO 2 RATE 4.5: a little slower than LFO 1.
- Listen for: a rich, moving shimmer.

steps.title: Soft strings
steps.why:
- FREQUENCY 6.5.
- Envelope 1 ATTACK 4, RELEASE 6.
- VOLUME 5.5: four chords of two oscillators are loud.
- Listen for: chords that bow in and fade.

steps.title: Chorus
steps.why:
- CHORUS LEVEL 7, MODE 2.
- Listen for: a wide ensemble.

context.osc1.shapeMod: In this sound: the depth of the shimmer.
context.fx.chorusLevel: In this sound: the ensemble width.

tweaks.try: Turn both SHAPE MOD knobs to 0
tweaks.hear: The shimmer stops and the strings turn into a still organ.

sounds.name: Velocity Keys
sounds.blurb: Punchy house chords whose brightness follows how hard each is played.
sounds.how: The Filter Freq route takes Envelope 2 scaled by Velocity, so harder chords snap the filter further open. Envelope 1's VELOCITY makes them louder too.

steps.title: Saw and pulse
steps.why:
- OSC BALANCE 0, OSC 2 WAVE pulse, OCTAVE +1.
- Listen for: a bright, piano-like spread.

steps.title: Velocity on the filter
steps.why:
- MODE LP24, FREQUENCY 4.
- CONTROL Filter Freq, SCALE Velocity, FREQ MOD 4.
- Envelope 2 DECAY 4, SUSTAIN 2.
- Listen for: soft chords dull, hard ones bright.

steps.title: Velocity on the loudness
steps.why:
- Envelope 1 VELOCITY 3, DECAY 4, SUSTAIN 4.
- Listen for: hard chords louder and short.

context.vcf.cutoffMod: In this sound: how far a hard chord opens the filter.
context.env1.velocity: In this sound: how much louder a hard chord is.

tweaks.try: Set the Filter Freq SCALE to Full On
tweaks.hear: Every chord opens the same way, however hard it is played.

sounds.name: Noise Hats
sounds.blurb: Ticking hi-hats from noise through the steep high-pass, accented by velocity.
sounds.how: NOISE BALANCE turned fully to N hears only the noise. HP24 takes off everything but the hiss, and a short Envelope 1 with VELOCITY gives each hit its weight.

steps.title: Noise only
steps.why:
- NOISE BALANCE 10.
- Listen for: plain hiss.

steps.title: The steep high-pass
steps.why:
- MODE HP24, FREQUENCY 7, RESONANCE 2.
- Listen for: a thin, bright sizzle.

steps.title: Short, and by velocity
steps.why:
- Envelope 1 DECAY 2.5, SUSTAIN 0, RELEASE 1.
- VELOCITY 2.
- VOLUME 10: noise this thin needs it.
- Listen for: crisp ticks, louder on the beat.

context.vcf.cutoff: In this sound: how thin the hats are.
context.env1.decay: In this sound: closed or open.

tweaks.hear: Closed hats open into a longer splash.

sounds.name: Repeating Pulse
sounds.ref: In the style of minimal techno
sounds.blurb: Hold a note and it pulses by itself, a throbbing bass from a looping envelope.
sounds.how: REPEAT loops Envelope 1 while the key is held: it rises over ATTACK, falls over DECAY and starts again, so a held note turns into a pulse. The Filter Freq route on Envelope 1 opens the filter with each pulse.

steps.title: A saw and its sub
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SUB LEVEL 6.
- Listen for: a deep saw.

steps.title: Loop the loudness
steps.why:
- Envelope 1 REPEAT lit.
- ATTACK 0, DECAY 3.
- Listen for: a held note pulsing over and over.

steps.title: The filter pulses with it
steps.why:
- FREQUENCY 4, RESONANCE 5.
- CONTROL Filter Freq, SOURCE Env 1, FREQ MOD 2.
- Listen for: each pulse a little wah.

context.env1.decay: In this sound: the speed of the pulse.
context.env1.repeat: In this sound: what makes it pulse.

tweaks.hear: The pulse slows down to a throb.

sounds.name: Fusion Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of Jan Hammer
sounds.blurb: A gritty, gliding lead with vibrato that fades in on held notes and grows under the mod wheel.
sounds.how: Both oscillators' pitch routes take LFO 1 scaled by aftertouch, which the app's mod wheel stands in for: push it up for more vibrato, as Hammer leaned on his keys and pitch wheel. LFO 1's FADE brings the vibrato in after each note starts. Mono, with glide, through the steep low-pass with drive.

steps.title: Two saws, one voice
steps.why:
- OSC BALANCE 0, CENT 1.
- VOICING Mono, GLIDE 2.
- Listen for: a fat line sliding between notes.

steps.title: Steep and driven
steps.why:
- MODE LP24, FREQUENCY 6, RESONANCE 3, DRIVE 3.
- Listen for: a bright but rounded, gritty tone.

steps.title: Vibrato under the wheel
steps.why:
Both pitch routes start on LFO 1; their SCALE becomes aftertouch (the app's mod wheel).
- CONTROL Osc1 Pitch, SCALE Aftertouch; CONTROL Osc2 Pitch, SCALE Aftertouch.
- PITCH MOD 0.6 on both, LFO 1 RATE 6.5 (about 4.5 Hz).
- LFO 1 FADE −2: the vibrato fades in.
- Listen for: push the mod wheel up for vibrato on held notes.

steps.title: A lead envelope
steps.why:
- Envelope 1 RELEASE 3.
- REVERB LEVEL 2.
- Listen for: notes that ring on a little.

context.kbd.glide: In this sound: the slide between notes.

tweaks.hear: The vibrato is there on every note, without the wheel.
